title: ElasticSearch queries to pattern match against the Stix2 Indicator Pattern syntax.
description:
We need to improve our Python backend queries to an ElasticSearch DB.
Specificialy, we have a collection of around 100,000 `Stix2 Patterns ` (http://docs.oasis-open.org/cti/stix/v2.0/stix-v2.0-part5-stix-patterning.html)

A few examples include:
- [ipv4-addr:value = '198.51.100.1/32']
- [email-message:body_multipart[*].body_raw_ref.value LIKE '%script_'
- ([file:hashes.'SHA-256' = '13987239847...'] AND [win-registry-key:key = 'hkey']) WITHIN 120 SECONDS


Initially, you can start with basic `LIKE` queries, then grow to RegEx and eventually introduce algorithms to consider the persistence modifiers (`FOLLOWED BY` || `WITHIN X SECONDS`). There will never be more than ~100,000 rows.

description:
At my company (around 400 employees), we still haven't managed to get into a co-working and desk sharing mode. I want to develop a super simple app that allows for desk sharing. It will only be used by my employees. Below the full description. As you can see, it is extremely simple. No need for fancy design. I will favour cost efficient proposals.

Introduction:
The Desk Sharing App is a web-based application that allows employees to easily book desks and manage their office space. The app provides a convenient way to book and manage desk availability, as well as offering a range of other features that improve the user experience.

Front-End:
The front-end of the app will be designed to provide a user-friendly and intuitive interface, including the following features:

User registration: Users will be able to register with their email address. If the email address is associated with the company, they will receive a confirmation email that they need to click to confirm their account.

Desk registration: Once users have registered, they will need to create a profile that includes their standard desk where they spend most of their time, as well as the days of the week they are there.

Dashboard: The dashboard will be a calendar that shows for each day where the user is sitting. There are four options per day: "At my desk", "In home office", "At desk xyz", or "On holidays/business trip". Users can click on each day and change where they sit, i.e. they can change it to any of the four options.

Desk booking: Users can select a location and date to see a list of available desks for that day. They can then book a desk from the available options.

Booking rules: There will be some rules, such as the maximum number of days in advance that users can book, and the requirement for administrator approval for long-term bookings or bookings in certain locations.

Check-in: Users need to check in if they go to another desk, but not if they go to their own desk. QR codes will be placed on all desks that users can scan to check in, or they can check in through the app.

Check-in reminders: Users will receive an email early in the morning on days where they have a booking.

Desk availability algorithm: There will be an algorithm that updates the database based on user registrations, bookings, check-ins, and other rules. For example, if a desk is not checked in within one hour, it will be released.

title: Algorithm to solve a Waste Collection Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows
description:
We are trying to solve a Waste Collection Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows and we hope you can help us find a solution.

For the problem we have the following requirements:
- All vehicles must leave and return to depot (there can be multiple depots)
- All nodes must be serviced only once
- The vehicle must be empty when starting a route and empty when it returns to depot
- Vehicles can unload at a disposal multiple times during the route
- Unloading a vehicle adds additional time to the route
- All vehicles have to work in a x hours time window (depart time, unload time and return to depot time included)
- Some of the nodes may have to be serviced in a specific time window (most of the time they don't have a time window)
- Every node has a service time, which can be different for each node
- All nodes accumulate demand except for the disposal sites and depots
- All vehicles have a capacity, which can be different for each vehicle
- Each vehicle must work in a distinct zone (routes should never intersect each other)

We have the following data:
- Nodes with longitude, latitude, service time, demand and optionally a time window
- One or more depots with longitude and latitude
- Disposal sites with longitude and latitude
- Vehicles with capacity and time window
- A distance and time matrix

Our aim is to reduce as much as possibile the overall solution distance and travel time while keeping distinct zones.

title: Web Development QAQC
description:
Web Development QAQC

Job Summary:

The Web Development QAQC will work as a part of a team of developers and designers to ensure that web applications and websites are of the highest quality before they are released to the public. This individual will be responsible for developing and executing test plans, identifying defects and issues, and working with the development team to ensure that all issues are resolved before release.

Responsibilities:

- Develop and execute test plans and test cases for all web applications and websites
- Work with the development team to identify and resolve defects and issues
- Ensure that all features and functionality of the web applications and websites are working as intended
-Collaborate with the development team to ensure that all aspects of the web applications and websites are of the highest quality
-Maintain documentation of all testing activities and test results
-Participate in the design and development of web applications and websites, providing input on quality issues and concerns
-Communicate with project stakeholders to provide updates on testing progress and results

Requirements:

-Experience with web application and website testing
-Experience with testing tools and techniques
-Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
-Excellent communication and collaboration skills
-Ability to work in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment
-Attention to detail and commitment to quality

Challenge: Develop a test plan and execute it to ensure the quality of a web application or website.

Details:

Choose a web application or website to test. You can use a project you've worked on in the past, or find an open-source project online to use for testing.

Develop a comprehensive test plan that includes test cases for the following aspects of the application or website:

1. Functionality: Does the application or website perform all its intended functions correctly?
2. Usability: Is the application or website user-friendly? Is it easy to navigate and use?
3. Compatibility: Does the application or website work well across different devices and browsers?
4. Performance: Does the application or website load quickly and respond in a timely manner?
5. Security: Is the application or website secure, and are user data and information protected?
6. Execute the test plan and document the results. Use a testing tool or framework to automate some of the testing, where appropriate.

Analyse the test results and report any defects or issues to the development team. Collaborate with the team to resolve any issues found.

Update the test plan and repeat the testing process to ensure that all defects and issues have been resolved.

Provide a final report to the development team summarizing the testing process, results, and any improvements made to the application or website.

This challenge will help the candidate demonstrate their ability to develop a comprehensive test plan, execute it, and work collaboratively with the devel

title: Data Analyst
description:
The Data Ninja job description includes, but is not be limited to:

Setting up measurements that allow for the tracking and collecting of data from various sources into Salesforce and/or Google Sheets (or any other system in use at the time)
Analysing and interpreting company data and promotional data collected, including measurements collected to track sales & marketing pathways
Creating reports and dashboards on Salesforce and/or Google Sheets to present data findings to the Data Manager
Reporting the data results to relevant Project Managers and/or Team Leaders on various teams 
Identifying patterns and trends in data sets and using this information to help Project Managers / Team Leaders to make better decisions
Defining new data collection and analysis processes required and assist with the successful implementation thereof
Working alongside the Data Manager to establish and execute on business data developments and data needs
Following the systems development life cycle in order to implement data systems / data automations that serve the data team and the company as a whole:
Planning
Systems Analysis
Development
Integration & Testing
Implementation
Operations & Maintenance
Disposal of Old with the New System
Continuously seeking to discover better systems / processes that can assist the data team with working smarter and with more ease by implementing data tracking automations that work and are cost effective
Creating and managing calendars on Google Calendar and Basecamp
Supporting the team with administrative & scheduling tasks as needed

The Data Ninja will require knowledge and experience of the following systems / programs:

Salesforce CRM - compulsory
Calendly
JIRA, Confluence, & Basecamp
Google Workspace (formerly G Suite)
Google Analytics
Facebook Analytics
YouTube Analytics
Linkedin Analytics
Social Media Platforms: Facebook, Linkedin, Twitter, Instagram, YouTube

The Data Ninja will require the following skills:

1. Creativity: Statistical analysis is only one part of the job. A data ninja needs to activate their creative spirit that pushes them to experiment, remain flexible and solve problems with a new, fresh perspective. And though there’s plenty of solo work time, the data ninja will have to be able to share knowledge and collaborate as a team member.

2. Curiosity: A data ninja must be able to look for the meaning or the “why” behind the numbers. With an insatiable drive to discover actionable insights, the data ninja must constantly ask questions and search for solutions. 

3. A strategic perspective: A data ninja must be able to dig into the numbers without losing sight of the bigger picture. A data ninja has to keep the goals and outcomes top of mind, and yet still be able to use the data to serve the company in the best way they know how.

4. Effective communication skills: Great data ninjas understand how to transform meaningful data into digestible insights and how to communicate those insights to everyone on the team,

title: Real-time skeleton-bound mesh animation
description: Its about a real-time animation. This is represented by an animation recording of an extraction skeleton consisting of 25 points. This extraction skeleton is bound to a 3D mesh. A mesh is a wireframe model that describes its surface through its points and triangles. You would have to create this mesh under Blender and attach it to the necessary skeleton corresponding to the one in the animation file. Then you would export the mesh with all its vertices, materials and skeleton information into your C++ program to be created and animate it there with Vulkan. For the implementation you would use C++, Vulkan and GLSL shaders. Vulkan is a low level API that allows you to communicate directly with your graphics card and generate graphics there.

1.	Authentication: Developers can use the API to authenticate users and generate access tokens that allow them to interact with the user's WhatsApp account.

3.	Message templates: Developers can create message templates to send structured messages to users, such as appointment reminders, shipping notifications, or reservation confirmations.
4.	WhatsApp Business APIs: Developers can use the WhatsApp Business APIs to interact with businesses and automate customer support tasks such as sending product information, order confirmations, and support messages.
5.	Message statistics: Developers can retrieve message statistics such as delivery status, read receipts, and timestamps.
6.	WhatsApp groups: Developers can use the API to create, manage, and retrieve information about WhatsApp groups.
7.	User profile information: Developers can retrieve profile information about WhatsApp users, such as their name and profile picture.
8.	Business profile information: Developers can retrieve business profile information, such as the business name, address, and hours of operation.
9.	Labels: Developers can use labels to categorize conversations and automate message routing based on conversation topics.
10.	Broadcast lists: Developers can create and manage broadcast lists to send messages to multiple recipients simultaneously.
11.	URL Shortener: Developers can use WhatsApp's URL shortener to shorten URLs in messages.
12.	Multi-device support: Developers can use the API to interact with WhatsApp accounts across multiple devices.
13.	Two-factor authentication: Developers can enable two-factor authentication to provide an extra layer of security for WhatsApp accounts.
14.	Multimedia and file sharing: Developers can share multimedia files such as images, videos, and audio files, as well as document files such as PDFs and Word documents.
15.	WhatsApp Web: Developers can use the WhatsApp Web interface to interact with WhatsApp accounts from a web browser.
16.	Status updates: Developers can retrieve information about user status updates and share their own status updates.

title: Laravel Vue Developer Needed to Help Finish Web App
description:
Hi everyone, I'm from London and I've been building a web app (Laravel backend, Vue frontend). I'm looking for a developer to help me finish the MVP and launch. I've worked in startups before, had CTO's, and many of my friends are developers. 

Here's a quick Loom Video showing the Web App - 
https://www.loom.com/share/df7907c39c424813a4335da2958a8d8d

OVERVIEW
- It's a therapy web app (single page application) which allows clients to log in and carry out their treatment with a therapist and access various resources like questionnaires. 

- I plan on launching an MVP asap but need some features built as well as finishing off various bits of functionality and so I'm looking for a developer to help with this. 
- I'm interested in forming a working relationship so  future dev work can be carried out too.

- Currently I'm looking mainly  for functionality and not UI/design CSS stuff. I can do these bits myself and so am hoping the developer can get the features working and I can then 'make it look pretty'.

FEATURES NEEDED 
As it's an MVP I'd like to use 3rd party integrations rather than build from scratch:

- Chat/Messaging - Was thinking Twilio, SendBird or CometChat

- Questionnaires - I have already built them in Typeform and so need to pass them through the app and deliver the results

- Zoom Integration with booking (Calendly)
- Stripe Payment Integration

- Mood Tracking - User fills out a Typeform (already setup) each week and the webapp shows the score changes over time

- Other more general things that can be discussed together

CURRENT TECH STACK
Backend - Laravel 9, Sanctum and Fortify for Auth, Laravel Nova 4 (being used as an admin panel), MySQL, Axios

Frontend - Vue 3, Vue Router, Vuex, Tailwind,  TailwindUI, Headless UI, Heroicons 

Deployment - Laravel Forge with Digital Ocean
(The code all currently sits in a private github account)

NEXT STEPS
I'd love to discuss the scope of what's needed and how it could be achieved in the most efficient manner. I see us starting with one or two of the features to see how it all goes and using slack as our communication platform throughout.

Many thanks, Tom

title: Update React Web App Integrating OpenAI and Midjourney AI Bots to e-commerce and NFT platforms
description:
We are seeking an experienced developer to join our team and assist with updating our react web app. The primary goal of this project is to integrate OpenAI and Midjourney AI Bots into our existing web application. The app will provide users with a range of prompt methodologies for the AI systems, enabling them to generate unique content and upload directly to ecommerce and NFT platforms.

DETAILS -
With this update, users will have four main prompt methodologies to choose from. These methodologies include single input, list input, theme-based prompts, and photo editing. In the first methodology, users will be able to provide a sentence as input, which will generate a response from the AI system. This approach will include a list of prompts that users can choose from by clicking on them. In the second methodology, users will be able to input multiple lists, and the AI system will cycle through them, creating a combination of inputs and outputs that will generate a large number of images.

The third methodology will enable users to input a general theme, which will be used by GPT-3 to provide input options to the user. The user can then select the prompts they want to use and output. The final methodology will allow users to upload photos for editing. The AI system will use DALLE, and the user will also be able to edit the photo based on their input.

With DALLE, we will have to make API requests, and with Midjourney, we will need to manage requests to and from their Discord. It is worth noting that Midjourney does not have the "upload photos for edit" functionality.

Once the user has selected their images and chosen either ecommerce or NFT channels (or both), they will be presented with per-product forms that they can fill in to specialize their product titles, descriptions, and provide other information, such as pricing. There will also be an option to take all the data inputted, such as the prompt and the type of item the design is being sold on, and make an intriguing product title and description.

The payment process will be handled through Stripe, with options for per-image or a percentage of NFT and ecommerce sales, which must be tracked on the app and billed monthly to our users. The app will handle automatic product uploads to Opensea and Printful, with a similar approach to automation.merchtitans.com by web scraping. The printful integration will require users to upload a product template with the correct positioning, and the automated system will upload their custom AI-produced image to their store.

Finally, users will be able to directly upload the product or add the products to a section on their "drop/queue" manager. For example, NFTs are generally "dropped," where all the product uploads happen at once. Some ecommerce platforms, such as Etsy, require a delayed upload, and therefore our users should put their products in a queue that uploads their products at a random interval set by the user.

title: Developer needed to help complete web app (JavaScript/Python)
description:
We are on a journey to help people decarbonise their homes. We are developing software that can provide bespoke energy analysis, helping people inform their decisions to lower their carbon footprint. We are linking our energy model to a web app and need help closing out the web page design. 

We are a team of two engineers with 20+ years experience, we have some skill in coding but are looking for help to get an MVP over the line. 

The task would be to assist us coding areas of the web page, allowing for a smooth customer journey through the site. 

The first task is to help us with data representation on the front end. The data is a compilation of results from a multi-variable analysis, many permutations are calculated and passed to view for representation. (See the attached image for a conceptual idea of how data should be represented.)

Data is passed to the view as a json where each key contains data about a particular permutation. (See the attached json file titled “jsonstructure.json”, in this case only one key is contained at the top level).Each key will hold data (measures, results, cost) for a particular permutation. 

The user should be able to select from available measures (these are strategies for retrofitting the house) and the view should be updated accordingly. Because there is a coupling effect or interdependence between measures a simple addition at the front-end is not sufficient, consequently, the permutation containing the selected measures should be found and all information displayed should be updated without having to refresh the page.

The view should be dynamic, intuitive, easy to understand and navigate. The attached conceptual image is only that, a concept, suggestions are welcome. Ideally, the 3D image of the house should be interactive and capable of clearly showing which elements are suggested for upgrade. 

While methods and libraries are not defined it has been suggested that this can be achieved with a combination of three.js, D3.js and well, JavaScript obviously.

title: Chatgpt chatbot with integrated api's
description:
Dear future developer,
I hope this finds you well. My name is Jorge, and I came across your profile while searching for an experienced developer to help me bring my AI-powered sports analytics platform idea to life. The project, called NxtGen365, aims to provide accessible predictions and insights on player performance for various sports, leveraging AI and machine learning technologies.
Here's a brief overview of the platform's key features and desired functionalities:
Comprehensive analysis of multiple data sources, including past performance, physical condition, opposition, team dynamics, injury reports, and external factors such as weather and venue.
User-friendly interface offering clear predictions, engaging insights, and annotations that are easy to understand.
Integration of ChatGPT API to handle user queries and provide insights through engaging, conversational interactions.
Visually appealing data visualization elements to present insights and predictions effectively.
To achieve these goals, we'll need to incorporate several APIs and technologies, such as:
Sports data APIs (e.g., Sportradar, Stats Perform, FantasyData) for historical and real-time sports data.
Weather data APIs (e.g., OpenWeatherMap, Weatherbit, AccuWeather) to consider weather conditions and venue-related factors.
Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) tools like TensorFlow, PyTorch, or spaCy for data analysis and predictions.
OpenAI's ChatGPT API for conversational insights and enhanced user engagement.
Data visualization libraries, such as D3.js, Chart.js, or Highcharts.
Geolocation API (e.g., Google Maps Platform or Mapbox) for venue information and location-based insights, if needed.
I would greatly appreciate the opportunity to discuss this project further with you and explore the possibility of collaborating. If you're interested in learning more or have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out.
Looking forward to hearing from you soon.
Best regards,
Jorge

title: Build a system to manage a company's financial instruments
description:
I am looking to develop a system which enables me to build up a profile of financial instruments held by clients - the clients being Companies. 

Each company may have a number of financial instruments issued to finance their operations, such as shares, preferred shares, debt instruments etc. 

In the event of a company being sold there is a structure by which those instruments rank in order of priority of repayment / value. 

As an example (ranking by seniority)

1. Senior Debt
2. Junior Debt
3. Loan Notes
4. Preferred Equity
5. Shares

Within the examples above there may be additional rules, such as two types of Preferred Equity which pays equally when whole, but one instrument may take priority over the other if not whole.

Or within Shares it might be that some shares only share in the distribution of capital in the event of a certain amount of capital being available for distribution.

I would like to build a system that:

1. Has an easy user interface
2. Enables the creation of different instruments which are defined by a set of rules
3. Storage of this data for each company
4. graphical output to illustrate how the instruments interact

A second phase of the project would be to enable the allocation of all or parts of each instrument to entities that own them (could be funds, companies or individuals) such that an output could be produced which shows who would receive what value from each instrument in the event of a sale of the Company.

title: Reinforcement learning offline to online to maximize retention
description:
we have an online video game and we discovered by data analysis that retention is very influenced by the ability of the user to stay in the "flow". The game has not to be too difficult (rage quit) nor too easy (boring). This is true for new users and for more experienced ones.
We have started creating an algorithm that increases the difficulty (0 to 10) automatically every 15 seconds depending on the user winning or losing the match that lasts 2 mins - so 8 changes per match
We want to solve this with an RL algorithm to be used online in order to predict the right next-best difficulty to maximize retention which means
- if the user does another match (doesn't matter if he wins or loose!)
- the number of consecutive days the user opens the app to do other matches

We have intensive data that can be ported to CSV or queried through SQL and we can structure an SQL table just to have a real-time view of this problem once we switch to online . 

Goal: 
* implementing "the gym" to our specific observation
* investigate 2-3 policies such as PPO, A3C. Open to suggestions, 
* implementing state-of-the-art baselines of such policies
* monitoring/measuring the effectiveness of the RL/policies.

Not required:

- Knowledge of programming languages such as Python, R, and JavaScript

- Knowledge of database design and management

title: ThinkOrSwim Programming
description:
I sell OTM vertical spreads on a series of ETFs. 
Our current system makes use of the template shown in the attached file.
 
All of this is pretty self-evident except the timing of the last order.  It is set to be submitted if the underlying stock price is less than or equal to the short leg strike price of $360.  This is our ITM Protection order that let’s us sleep at night. This entire process is designed such that we can look at our account 1x per day and be confident things will be taken care of.  I am aware that there are other strategies to handle the stoplimit and the ITM protection that might improve our ROI but they require more attention to the trades than we are willing to provide. 
This template has been very successful for us so far but there is an unintended consequence that could occur and we would like to avoid it.  
As it stands, if the stock gaps overnight for example, it is possible that the StopLimit and the ITM Protection order would both trigger simultaneously, canceling the Profit Capture order.  TD Ameritrade has confirmed that in the event that happens one of the buy orders would get filled and the other buy order would remain active.  This could result in a purchase of the vertical spread at some unknown value.  
I am unaware of a way to alter the OCO order we have to fix this issue.  It has occurred to me that possibly some programming in Active Trader could execute the same template, but be conditioned such that if 2 orders triggered at the same time, the system would give preference to the ITM protection order and cancel both the StopLimit order and the Profit Capture order. 
I am an EE with computer background, but no longer have the programming skills or the desire to learn them to do this programming myself. 
If this is doable, let me know your thoughts.  I’d be willing to spend $100 to get this issue resolved.

title: Excel VBA data processing and reporting
description:
The excel spreadsheet will be protected by an NDA, so that can only be shared once a contract is signed. 

The requirements as a rough outline:

Data consist of date/time, position coordinates, "KP values (Kilometer point), sensor data from a machine moving along a path. Spreadsheet shall give a graph showing sensor data vs position along the path.

- Import multiple txt based files into Excel
- Option to append more files to the dataset later if forgotten to import earlier - and re-sorted into the existing data.

- Sort data based on KP / time. 

- Register (?) sections of continuous data, and make a table of dates, KP from, KP to, distance (depending on going on ascending or descending KP) for the whole dataset

- Filter data to avoid duplicate KP values. Should have one reading/line per meter (0.001 KP)

- Highlight any gaps in dataset (i.e. missing KP values). Present subsets of the gaps in a separate sheet, i.e. 10 lines leading up to the gap, and 10 following the gap, for operator to analyse easily in a graph.

- Potentially have an option to interpolate the KP and position data in the gaps and keep sensor values same (alarm if there are "big" differences, use threshold values to define this).

- Create QC graphs, dynamically - depending on how many data gaps there are. Update gap graphs if gaps are reprocessed and filled by interpolation, remove gap graph entirely if gap is filled by adding real data. Keep a QC table with info about ranges that have been interpolated.

- Create a feature to adjust certain sensor values within a range to account for errors in calibration or readings. Cut and paste original ranges into a separate table and show as dashed line in the graph, and overlay a solid line with final data. Keep a table of ranges manipulated for QC.

- Unless speed values are correctly logged in dataset, create a formula that calculates speed, and average speed. Need to take into account data going past midnight, and at times where machine has stopped, and restarted 2 days later etc, to avoid spikes in the data.

- Create feature to export positions to a given format.

- Add a column whereby user can add manual values based on KP, which then will be interpolated along the line - more details on this later

A separate project could come from this, where data that has been processed in this sheet, is pushed to a database in the cloud, and accessed by multiple Excel instances in different locations to read and publish to client. To be discussed separately.

title: PyTorch C++ Modifications
description:
We are translating inference program from Pytorch to Pytorch C++ frontend. The only thing is not implemented in C++ frontend is register_forward_hook function in the torch::nn::module part. It was requested years before but was triaged "not urgent and not important" by dev team.

The goal is to implement this feature so that we could use it in our project.
You can see status of API parity for Python and C++ with implementation notes here: https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/25883

The interesting issues and PR from github is here:
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/25888 - Here is where you can see the prioritization from developers.
https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/26568 - Here you find how register_hook for at:Tensor implemented in C++ API

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/29037 - register_forward_hook support for TorchScript.

https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/pull/30484 - register_forward_pre_hook PR example (failed to merge with master)

for more information please see this

https://pytorch.org/cppdocs/

If you dive into this archive you can see that there are only C++ headers and natively compiled libraries

https://download.pytorch.org/libtorch/nightly/cpu/libtorch-shared-with-deps-latest.zip

title: C# RabbitMQ and MassTransit On Windows Developer
description:
Need someone with experience in working with C# .NET 7, RabbitMQ and MassTransit to create a couple of Windows apps.

Milestone 1: A Windows Console client app in .NET 7 that adds a SampleRunApp Class to a "run-app" queue or adds SampleBrowseWeb Class to a "browse-website" queue based on command line arguments received when started. If no arguments supplied, output a help to show what command line arguments are valid.

Milestone 2: A Windows server app in .NET 7 that watches for the SampleRunApp class in the "run-app" queue and for SampleBrowseWeb class to the "browse-website" queue. The app should be able to handle multiple threads at one time. The limit to the number of messages at one time should be defined in a config file.

Milestone 3: Create a docker image for the Windows Server that has Windows 11 on it along with Edge and Chrome browsers. The docker image should be started by the Windows server app when a message is received in the "run-app" queue or "browse-website" queue.

Milestone 4: When the server app receives a "SampleRunApp" message and it launches the docker image, it should install the app specified and launch the app. Capture the UI inside the docker image which should be the app to the Windows Server C:\Screens folder with the filename being "browse-scn-" + datetime including milliseconds. For the POC, the app should be the console app from milestone 1.

Milestone 6: When the server app has finished processing the message in milestone 4 or 5 and the docker image has closed, the server app should send a message back to the producer app that the message was processed. When the app in milestone 1 receives this message, it can exit.

Milestone 7: Modify the app in milestone 1 to send a "ScheduleBrowse" to a queue "schedule-browse". The command line arguments should accept a time and how often that will be send as part of the message. How often should be one of the following, "Daily", "Weekly" or "Monthly".

Milestone 8: The server app, milestone 2, should be modified to watch the "schedule-browse" queue. When a message is received, it should use Quartz.NET to setup a scheduler that runs based on the time information in the message. When it runs, it will perform the same functionality as milestone 7 for launching a docker image to browse the url specified and capture the screen of the docker image to the windows server folder.

title: Rust : Quickest way to make HTTPS requests
description:
We are looking to make HTTPS requests in Rust, in the mind to make the quickest one request possible.

Reqwest, Hyper, and other high level library are not quick enough, taking too much time. Right now our setup is using a pre-opened TLS connection, and at the required time, use that to send the request. 
You can see our, so far, working example attached.

We are requesting worldtimeapi(.)org/api/timezone/Europe/London and compare the responded time (utc_datetime) with the moment we sent it to know how slow is the request made to be build and sent. Of course, we are comparing on the same server, with the same network, etc.

The goal is either :
Have a pool of pre-opened TLS connections and pull one when needed (the time to get one of the poll can slow down the process)
Keep one TLS connection and re-used it.

Of course, we must read the response without blocking the thread. Use of Tokio because we are in a multi-thread program, but we are not close to use lazy_static or other global ref.
The need to pass header / body is obvious, as well as GET / POST, but it can be pre-built to gain time (already in a pre-created request, connection).

We are open to suggestion, if you have a better idea and improve this code, we will be open to add bonus to the job.

PS: If you want to be hired, you must show that you know Rust and the subject, generic message will be ignored.

title: NODE application that accepts Wix Stores webhooks requests
description:
The application must be a NODEJS app (in TypeScript or JS ES6) and it should answer to 2 Wix Stores order webhook requests, preferably using ExpressJS.

These are the hooks:
- Fulfillment Created Webhook [API docs](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/wix-stores/orders/fulfillment-created-webhook)
- Fulfillment Updated Webhook [API docs](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/wix-stores/orders/fulfillment-updated-webhook)

The application should then:
- Get the Wix Stores `orderId` and retrieve its order object [API docs](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/wix-stores/orders/get-order)
- If that order has `fulfillmentStatus` as `FULFILLED` it should then:
    - Find the corresponding property from the Wix Store objects that corresponds with Vipps order id.
    - Then initiate a **full amount** capture with VIPPS (a Norwegian payments provider) [API docs](https://vippsas.github.io/vipps-developer-docs/docs/APIs/ecom-api/vipps-ecom-api#capture) and in detail [here](https://vippsas.github.io/vipps-developer-docs/api/ecom#tag/Vipps-eCom-API/operation/capturePaymentUsingPOST).

The application should implement the necessary logic for dealing with the authorization and/or token validation methods with both APIs.

### Definition of Done
The task is considered complete if all the described steps are implemented.

*This is a pseudo-application. That is: we just want the theoretical code that would be needed for the application to run if it were published.

I am building out an app where local businesses can keep track of and encourage return customers.

—

- The ability to create an account as either an Admin (business owners) or a Customer

- Admins must be able to create a profile for their business with basic business info (name, location, etc.) as well as a place where they list Rewards they offer

Rewards take the format of “Purchase [service] [# of times] and receive [reward] for [free product / % discount on service]” 

Rewards must also be defined by the Admin as “Only to be used once” or “Can be used multiple times” (i.e. after a Customer gets the reward once, can they restart the Reward program)

- Custom app links and QR codes for all business pages so a Customer can easily find the business page they’re looking for

- When a Customer wants to use a Reward, the Admin must be able to authenticate that 1 out of [total #] of the services has been used and this must be saved and shown in the app to both the Admin and Customer

- When a Customer uses all the services of a Reward, the Reward must be archived and marked as used in their account

VERSION 2:

Integration with Square, Stripe, etc. to process service payments directly in app

More complex rewards programs

Analytics for Admin

To be considered please answer the following: 
(1) how long would it take you to build Version 1?
(2) how much would it cost?

(4) please provide a rough breakdown on how you would build this out and how long each part would take.

title: Qualtrics Expert for Javascript and JQuery Coding
description:
We are a team of social scientists seeking an experienced Javascript and JQuery coder for a Qualtrics survey development. This survey is one component of a larger project using images to study hiring discrimination against minorities. For this survey, we are developing a measure of attractiveness using over 100,000 images.


Responsibilities

There are two primary responsibilities included for this work. (1) The coder will work with our team experimentalist on the survey development. Working together will include collaborating and providing access to the survey, answering any questions for the coder, and pilot testing the survey. (2) The coder will be responsible for developing display logic for a set quota across individual survey items. 

More specifically, the survey contains 100,000+ images. We have set a quota for each image to only be displayed 5x within the survey for participants to rate the images. After 5 participants have seen and rated an image, it will be removed from the pile of available images. As opposed to adding display logic for the quota to each individual photo, the coder will develop a global code using Javascript and/or JQuery based on the quota. The code would remove or hide an image after 5 ratings, or once the quota is complete.


Skill Requirements 

	Proficiency in scriptwriting (i.e., Javascript and/or JQuery)
	Proficiency in Qualtrics 
o	Quota Logic 
o	Display Logic


If you have experience using Qualtrics, coding for Qualtrics, and a passion for using data to drive research, we encourage you to apply for this exciting opportunity to work with our team!

description: Our business allows customers to pay to have old audio tapes, video tapes and images digitized. The customer will add the products to their cart and pay to have their items digitized. We then ship the customer a box for their items and they ship them to us and we digitize them and ship them back to them. Once the customer has put the products in their cart and they are getting ready to checkout we need an option to ask the customer how they would like to receive the digital files (i.e. on a CD/DVD, a thumb drive, a YouTube private playlist and/or digital download/cloud). The customer must be required to choose one of these options in order to checkout and they should be able to choose as many of these options as they want, but they have to choose at least one option. Each of those options will have a price and as the number of items the customer puts in the cart increases so should the price of each of these options. In other words, if the customer puts 10 items in their cart and they choose the option to get the digital files back on a thumb drive, the price for the thumb drive option might be $19.99 added to the total price and if they also want to get the files on a CD/DVD that would add another $19.99 to the total. If the customer put 20 items in their cart then the price for the thumb drive should go to $39.99. So, the price of these addon options should increase with a specific number of products in the cart. If you think the budget for this is too low then make an offer. We might have some flexibility with the budget, depending. I have attached several files to hopefully give an example of the functionality.

title: Web designer needed with Figma, Webflow, and Entrepreneurial experience
description:
BetaBlox is THE digital agency for entrepreneurs. Everything we build comes from over a decade of battle-tested entrepreneurial experience. We run a successful startup incubator, have invested in hundreds of companies, and produce a reality TV show on entrepreneurship called The Blox. We help our customers scale and grow, and right now we are growing OUR TEAM with the addition of our next top-notch, bad-to-the-bone, get-shit-done Web Designer. 

Is that you? Awesome. Read on!


What You'll Be Doing
========================================
We make beautiful custom websites for each client. You'll be creating these amazing web experiences from start to finish. That means helping us meet with clients, discuss business requirements, collect assets, designing drafts, tweaking designs with feedback, and of course developing and publishing to the world.

But the unsung hero of our business is the process we use to make each project better (and faster) than the last. Here's a our process in a nutshell:

(Step 1) Collect.  Meet with the client, discuss requirements, and start gathering business details & logo, images, service & product information, testimonials, text, video, audio, and anything else needed to build their website.

(Step 2) Compose. Design websites with strong attention to detail based on client vision and feedback. Be prepared to work through a few rounds of revision and feedback. Some clients are easy going, others demand high quality.

(Step 3) Create. Build and launch top-tier website experiences. We only develop custom websites, nothing copy and pasted from generic (and boring) templates. Additionally, we expect clients to stay with us for years to come, so you must create with future changes in mind.

(Step 4. Care) Launching the website is just the beginning, we also handle hosting, maintenance, plugins, performance, security, etc. Our goal is for clients to become long-term web partners, and every team member should work to foster that kind of relationship.

Some responsibilities you will be expected to assume are:
=============================================
- Create wireframes or mockups for websites
- Design websites for mobile, tablet, and desktop devices
- Design custom Webflow websites
- Ongoing research and evaluation of new design trends
- Meet weekly with clients to discuss their project and tweak website designs


Skills You Will Need
========================================
- Figma for designing websites
- Webflow for developing websites
- Demonstrable web design skills with a strong portfolio
- Extremely effective time management skills, self-motivation, and discipline
- You highly value communication, documentation, and are willing to devote time and effort to both activities throughout the week.


Why This Job Might Not Be For You

description:
We are a multi-tenant B2B2C SaaS platform offering web-based free-to-play games. We have a need to better track game play conversions so that this data can be leveraged in both Sales opportunities and client education. 

We're looking to leverage Google Analytics to answer basic questions such as: 
* What is our "overall" conversion rate?
* What is our conversion rate when users enter from various sources (defined by UTM codes)? 
* Where do users drop of the conversion flow? 
* What steps in our flow create the most friction for users? 

The chosen hire should have experience with multi-tenant applications. We are looking for expertise on best practices, i.e.:
* To properly separate traffic data, should a separate GA4 tag be used for each client? 
* As a single page application, how are Analytics tags best applied? 

Milestones include: 
* Delivery of assessment of current Google Analytics setup on all pages of our web-based application
* Delivery of suggested user paths and actions that should be tracked
* Strategy for implementation 
* Prioritization of these tactics, with consideration for level of effort (we can crawl, walk, run, if necessary)
* Implementation of proposed GA setup and tagging
* Ongoing monitoring with regular review of data for accuracy and improvement opportunities

We are hopeful to complete the initial assessment, strategy and implementation within 3-5 weeks. Ongoing monitoring will continue after that.

About the Foundation for Sickle Cell Disease Research

We are fighting a battle for people living with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD). The Foundation for Sickle Cell Disease Research (FSCDR) is the United States’ first outpatient center exclusively dedicated to the treatment of and innovative research for SCD. Florida has the highest population of individuals living with SCD in the U.S. In 2012, we opened our first center in Hollywood, FL, offering focused care and collecting data through clinical trials. We utilize a human-centric, community-based, rigorously scientific approach to caring for our patients and finding better solutions to treat them.

For the past ten years, we have grown strong roots in the South Florida community and have taken great strides toward our mission of resetting the narrative around SCD through specialized care and innovative research.

We are focused on helping people living with SCD—offering more support to our patients, their families, and the broader sickle cell trait and advocate communities, while creating a center for collaborative research that encourages scientists, medical professionals, and physicians researching and treating SCD to work toward new, life-improving solutions.

We are a woman-owned and black-owned organization and we are expanding! We have big
plans in store!

title: Web3 Developer needed for new Web3 Protocol
description:
Introduction:
This project involves the front-end development and smart contract integration of the Risecoin protocol (on the Binance Smart Chain testnet).

Project Goals:
1. Front-end development of a UI similar to Morpho Labs - https://www.morpho.xyz/ and Morpho-Compound - https://compound.morpho.xyz/?network=mainnet
2. Integration with the smart contracts that we already developed. Specifically, the smart contract functions for integration can be found in the Morpho.sol smart contract - https://github.com/morpho-dao/morpho-v1/blob/main/src/compound/Morpho.sol. Integration work will be done on our version of the same smart contract on the Binance Smart Chain testnet. A library wrapper around the smart contract has already been created and is written in TypeScript - https://github.com/morpho-labs/morpho-ethers-contract. This can be used to easily integrate with the smart contract by plugging in the right smart contract address.
3. Host the front end on a cloud provider, e.g., AWS
4. Build scripts for smart contract event listeners to be integrated into the front-end (optional - depending on budget and time) - the scripts will poll the smart contract for events, store these events in the database, and update the data displayed on the front-end, i.e., stats about activated assets or markets on-chain.

Deliverables:
1. UI/UX development or a way to scrape the Morpho UI code and build something similar.
2. Front-end development and hosting on Vercel.
3. Smart contract integration.

title: Fix Shopify Backend Custom Registration (php to liquid)
description:
Currently we have a custom registration process on our Shopify site. When visitors go to the registration page they have two options (see attached step1.png):

1. (left-side) They insert a unique membership code. The code they insert could be all kinds of characters and it should not be case sensitive. So if we have the term "BenefitHub" as the membership code users can insert "benefithub" or "BENEFITHUB" or "BeNEfItHuB" they should be able to see the next step in the registration process. See all unique codes in our Apps/Accentuate Custom Fields/Shop/Edit Values. 

2. (right-side) They are a member of military, medical, first responder, teacher and they use SheerID to verify their membership with those associations. When SheerID sends back a successful response only then we consider the visitor as verified.

Once a visitor is successfully verified, by either left or right side verification option, then they are shown the account creation form (first & last name, email, password) to open a Shopify account. (see attached step2.png).

Once they have successfully created their account it is important that we store in their customer profile on Shopify how they registered. If they used a membership code (left-side) then in the customer tags we should see the membership code they used (in all caps) as well as the word 'VERIFIED'. If they registered with SheerID (right-side) then we need to see the kind of association they are a part of also in all caps (basically which button they clicked), "MILITARY" or "TEACHER" or "MEDICAL" or "FIRST RESPONDER" as well as the words "SHEERID" and "VERIFIED".


***Here is the problem we need to fix***
Currently all this is working through a php file which I will provide to you. We do not wish to host this logic on any server, but would prefer that we keep this within Shopify. If we could convert the php logic into Shopify's liquid code that would be ideal. For the membership code (left-side) I don't mind us putting the codes right into the form as a validation to show step2 if that will make it easier. We are not concerned about someone seeing the source code of this form and getting a membership code the wrong way. 

I want to make sure that the SheerID (right-side) verification can be done from within Shopify, without the need to use external php script. 

Also currently we save some SheerID information (like their unique verification id) in the Shopify customer profile meta fields. We like having it, but it is not necessary at all.

title: MVP: ChatGPT Knowledge Base
description:
Hi, I want to build an MVP for a knowledge base that can be queried using the latest LLM models. Doesn't have to be ChatGPT. 

Here's the main happy flow user story: 

MVP: I can upload documents and then ask questions about those documents in a chat interface similar to ChatGPT. 

- We can start with a proof of concept of just one document. I can show you a reference application.

Here's my simple idea how to do it:
- Upload document, then extract text out of document, then feed into OpenAI API with the correct prompts. 

- There will be two issues; 
1. the API has a token limit so that will limit how much you can feed in and how much it can reply, and 
2. it won't remember the previous messages in the chat. 

Some are using Pinecone as "memory" by putting the embeddings in a database, which can work for semantic search, but not sure if that works to feed back into the OpenAI API. 

I'm looking for someone who is familiar with working with the latest LLM models and can do basic web development.

This dashboard provides an at-a-glance view of the alarms that have been triggered most frequently over the previous week, and also shows how many alarms were opened in total during that time period. The line chart provides a way to track the overall trends in alarm activity over time. 

Also need to  find out which days have more alarms and what the average number of alarms per day is

In this example, the dashboard shows the following additional information:

    The number of alarms triggered on each day of the previous week: A stacked bar chart shows the number of alarms triggered on each day of the previous week, with each color representing a different alarm.
    An average number of alarms per day: A separate metric shows the average number of alarms triggered per day over the previous week.

With these additional visualizations, users can now see which days had more alarms than others and the average number of alarms per day. This information can help users identify patterns or trends in alarm activity and take appropriate actions to address any issues or concerns.

Monitor changes over time: You can monitor changes in the number of alarms triggered over time to identify trends or patterns. For example, you can compare the number of alarms triggered this week to the number triggered in the previous week to see if there has been an increase or decrease in activity. This can help you identify potential issues before they become major problems.

title: Navigation Page for a 3D Matterport Space
description:
As a developer, you are tasked with creating a navigation page for a Matterport Space using the Matterport SDK. The configuration for the Matterport space will be loaded from a config file in the folder. Page should work in any folder online with normal hosting, or as an iframe / embedded in a CMS

The page will feature a set of navigational controllers that will allow users to load certain positions of the space in the Matterport viewer. These controllers will be organized as either links or dropdown menus, which will be defined in the config file. The controllers will be placed underneath the Matterport Space viewer and will be organized in columns. The layout has to be adapting to screen size, also work on mobile devices

For links, the page will display the name of the link and the URL. When clicked, the link will take the user to the specified position in the Matterport Space. For dropdown menus, the page will display the dropdown name and a list of dropdown elements, each with its own link URL. When clicked, the dropdown element will take the user to the specified position in the Matterport Space.

The page should have a similar functionality to the yellow dots on the minimap in the example provided at https://matterport.github.io/showcase-sdk/sdk_navigation_controls.html, but instead of clicking on the minimap dots, users will interact with links or dropdown menus.
Example of link URLs should be in the following format:

https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&hhl=0&play=1&tiles=1&hl=0&sr=-3,1.05&ss=62
https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&hhl=0&play=1&tiles=1&hl=0&sr=-.22,-1.04&ss=55
The links and dropdown menus should be placed under the Matterport Space Viewer, with a maximum of three columns for dropdown menus and four columns for links.

Example of config file

Space = https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2

Dropdown 1 = Places (this is the name displayed on top of the Dropdown Menu)

Entrance: https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&sr=-3.07,1.42&ss=5
Host: https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&sr=-.88,1.45&ss=13
Bar: https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&sr=-3.06,-.02&ss=35

etc, Dropdown 2, 3 etc 
Entrance, Host and Bar are the items in the dropdown with the respective URLS)

Link:Bar: https://my.matterport.com/show/?m=cKHMpazixm2&sr=-3.06,-.02&ss=35

Will create a link Bar that when clicked will take to corresponding URL

title: Looking for a product team to work on continuous basis
description:
We are building an AI-powered web application that makes it easy for users to find the information they need to navigate the complex world of customs and trade compliance.

Current State
The initial version of the web application has been built using Laravel+VueJS and can be accessed at https://www.customsclearance.net/. Our goal now is to improve current functionality and build new features using more advanced technological solutions.

Content Discovery and Search
- The web application will use a machine learning model to personalize search results and recommendations based on various factors such as the user's website usage history, location, and industry. For example, if a user frequently searches for information about importing electronics from Japan, the AI could suggest articles or resources related to that topic or alert the user to any changes in customs regulations that may affect their shipments. The search engine will be able to access data not only from the CustomsClear database but also from other sources such as the Access2Market database, and show the most appropriate search results from verified and tested providers.

Translation
- The web application will use an AI-powered automated translation model to translate the content into the user's preferred language.
- This model will be specifically trained to work with customs and trade compliance terms, ensuring accurate and up-to-date translations.
- The goal is to start with several EU languages

Additional Specification
- For all AI-related functionality, 3rd party AI integration tools will be used.
- The development team will focus on building the core functionality of the web application while leveraging the latest AI technologies to provide fast and accurate responses to user queries and personalized recommendations.
- There will be an algorithm that automatically analyzes all incoming search requests as well as user behaviour on the website and generates reports and suggestions on describing trends and most requested topics. Basically helps to collect market intelligence and analyze demand (the hottest topics).

Possible 3rd party AI integration tools.
Personalized search and content recommendations:
·         Coveo 
·         Google Cloud Recommendation Engine: 
·         Amazon Personalize: 
·         Microsoft Azure Personalizer 
 Automated translation:
·         Google Translate:

We are looking for a product team that can help us to create the product described above. Send us a message and let's discuss the details and further steps.

title: Data analysis (ANOVA, descriptive statistics and correlation)
description:
The data analysis is regarding the agriculture experiment. Here I will give a brief explanation about the work I have done. 

We cultivated 72 cultivars of a crop in a field with no replications and 24 are harvested early, 24 are harvested intermediate and 24 are harvested lately.

The data I have provided has 72 different cultivars/varieties in which 24 are harvested early, 24 are harvested late and 24 are harvested intermediately. 

The purpose of this work is “ To know whether early, intermediate and late harvested cultivars differ in their germination success, biometry(seed length, width, area), TKG, yield related traits(Flowering time, pod width, pod length, plant height, seed colour and seed yield) ” 

For the germination test we performed 4 replications each cultivar is tested 4 times. For biometry we took 4 subsamples from each cultivar. For yield related traits we collected data manually. All these data are clearly provided in the excel file. 

With the provided data we have to do analysis to know whether there are any changes/differences  in germination success(%), Biometry parameters and yield related parameters between early, intermediate and late harvested cultivars. 

For data analysis: 

Descriptive statistics: Min, Max, Range, Mean and CV for early, intermediate and late harvested cultivars for all the parameters mentioned.

Different cultivars where harvested at different times, so it makes sense to calculate only the average of the measurements per cultivar  
and use this as the response variable in anova and harvesting time as the explanatory variable. 

So the model could be, 
eg: average grain weight per cultivar(parameter) ~ havesting time (ordinary linear model - anova)

all the parameters can be done like the above

Or anything as per your experience which suits for this experiment.

Evolving technology, competition, and workforce changes are making it difficult to find in-demand skills. It’s so difficult that nearly half of companies are getting critical work done by turning to freelancers.

Freelancers operate like a business. Posting a freelance job is like sending businesses a request for proposal: What you put into it affects what you get out of it. Your freelancer job post should provide enough information for talent to set the price, know they’re qualified, and confirm they can be available when you need the project done.

When writing a project description, you just need to remember RTT: Results, Targets, Time

description:
We are looking for a Blender developer with python experience, that can help us to create an automated system for doing cloud rendering.

We are creating a web portal where users can design their own custom designs of an object.
This might include chosing 1 of 5 texture files as well as selecting different RGB values.
Once happy, they will save their design choices and wait for an mp4 including their design choices.

This information can be saved to an online spreadsheet that has a unique user id, and their selections, which texture and RGB value, and if the shot has been rendered.

We are able to create an animation within blender and have it setup with lighting and camera moves as well as mapping any textures to the object, and optimising the renders.

We are looking for a developer to help us setup a system that can trawl through the spreadsheet and wait for a new user to submit their data.
Once it finds a new user it updates the blender scene, switching out the relevant texture file and tweaking RGB values on another material.
It then renders out the frame sequence using those values to a cloud folder with the users unique user ID, and updates the spreadsheet that it has been rendered.

if there are other listings in the sheet, then it progresses to update those too.

The system must be able to handle hundreds of requests and process them accordingly.

We are looking for an experience python developer who knows how to program for Blender automation.
Candidates must have examples of previous work.

title: ChatGPT Chatbot with OCR, SEO, and Fact-Checking Capabilities for Wordpress Website
description:
Objective: To create a chatbot interface for news website that can provide personalized and engaging responses to user queries and preferences. 
The chatbot should be able to access news articles and press releases, and be trained on historical user interactions to improve its understanding of user queries. 

Additionally, the project should include an OCR module to read press releases received via email as PDF and use ChatGPT to create articles about the content, a ChatGPT module to go through the entire database and add SEO to each article, and a fact-checking module to verify the accuracy of information in each article.

================================

Automating the Creation of News Articles from Emails

Develop an OCR module to read press releases received via email as PDF or plain text and create articles about the content in wordpress CMS.

Use the email service provider (ESP) API to import press releases and create articles about the content.

Train a ChatGPT model on the dataset extracted from the WordPress database, to create articles based on the information contained in emails.

Use the ChatGPT model to create articles about the content of emails, optimize the articles for SEO, and store them in the WordPress database.


Guest User Experience

Develop a chatbot interface integrated with the news website that provides personalized and engaging responses to user queries and preferences.

Use the ChatGPT model trained in the first task to improve the chatbot's understanding of user queries and preferences.

Develop a function in the chatbot that displays a welcome message to the user when they visit the website, and use a natural language processing (NLP) API like ChatGPT to analyze the user's input and provide a response that is relevant to their interests or past interactions with the website.

Use the NLP API or a keyword detection tool to determine if the user arrives on the website through a specific topic or article, and provide a topic-specific greeting message that offers the user more information on the topic or related stories.

Develop a function in the chatbot that prompts the user to ask a question or express their interests, and use the NLP API to analyze the user's input and provide a response that is relevant to their interests or requests.

Provide an option for users to add their email to continue with the chatbot and save their conversations.

More information will be provided to selected project developer.

title: Celery worker/consumer for AWS EventBridge Scheduler payloads
description:
We are looking for an experienced Python, Celery developer to create a Celery worker/consumer that will process scheduled messages off of an SQS queue. We would like to have something deployed in 1 - 1.5 weeks with 1 - 2 weeks of testing/tweaking.

Our current system schedules tasks with AWS EventBridge Scheduler which then puts a message onto SQS when it's time to be processed. Our consumer (Kombu) then pulls messages off the queue and processes the message. We would like to pivot to using Celery as it offers more robust capabilities. The work will be a complete re-write of the worker/consumer.

What differs between a typical Celery Worker/Consumer solution and our desired solution is that AWS EventBridge Scheduler will be placing the messages onto SQS and not a Celery app. From what we have read, this may require using bootsteps.ConsumerStep.

Tasks can run for up to 60 minutes, for this reason, the consumer should stop pulling tasks off of the queue when no processes are available.

title: TYPO3 developer needed for site update
description:
The task is to update an existing, outdated TYPO3 installation to the newest LTS version (11) on Composer while maintaining the outward output, styling and content

Given:
* Version = 7.6.30
* Some custom extensions
* Not using Composer
* Uses some custom templates
* IMPORTANT: outputs its content as XML for parsing by an external service. No direct HTML output.
* Uses: realurl v2.5.0
* Uses: tt_news v7.6
* Uses: bootstrap_core v1.2.8
* Uses: bootstrap_grids v1.3.1
* Uses: bootstrap_package v7.1.1
* Uses: css_styled_content v7.6.30
* Most (all?) pages make use of Bootstrap Grid, which outputs Bootstrap 3-compatible content.

You will be provided with an anonymized copy of the installation, excluding content files, and an anonymized copy of the database.

Task:
* the installation must be converted to Composer
* custom extensions must be converted to Composer modules
* (non-custom) TYPO3 extensions must be updated to the version required to be functional with the new TYPO3 version. If there is no compatible version, a functionally equivalent extension may be installed instead
* Move all templates, TS etc. from css_styled_content to fluid_styled_content. This also applies to the custom templates (included in the repository).

Deliverables:
* Git repository containing the updated installation and the commits used to reach the updated state
* A database dump of the updated installation
* A step-by-step guide containing the steps/commands necessary to update the installation from the old version to the new.

Acceptance criteria
* installation must be a functional TYPO3 v11 installation
* external-facing page URLs have not changed (will be checked with random pages and news items)
* page content has not changed (will be checked with random pages and news items)
* installation now uses Composer
* custom extensions are functional
* custom extensions are placed in folder packages/ in the root
* all non-custom extensions are NOT committed to the repository. Running "composer install" on a freshly checked out copy of the repository produces a working installation
